content: Green tea enhances the effects of norepinephrine through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the caffeine content, as the combination may increase central nervous system (CNS) stimulatory effects. Green tea, when combined with oxaprozin, paroxetine, piroxicam, prasugrel, ticlopidine, tirofiban, or sulindac, may increase the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Green tea may increase the effects of phendimetrazine, phentermine, pirbuterol, salmeterol, terbutaline, albuterol, formoterol, or arformoterol due to pharmacodynamic synergy. This is attributed to the caffeine content, which may enhance CNS stimulatory effects. Caffeine should be avoided or used cautiously. Green tea, when combined with phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, selegiline, selegiline transdermal, tranylcypromine, or yohimbine, may increase the risk of cardiac arrhythmias or severe hypertension due to the caffeine component. Avoiding the combination or excessive consumption of green tea is advised. Phenytoin decreases the levels of green tea by increasing its metabolism, potentially reducing the effects of caffeine. Caution and monitoring are advised. Green tea increases the effects of theophylline by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended due to the caffeine content. Verapamil increases the levels of green tea by decreasing its elimination, likely through inhibition of hepatic metabolism. Patients should be advised to limit or minimize the intake of caffeinated products to reduce caffeine-related side effects. Green tea decreases the effects of benzodiazepines such as alprazolam, chlordiazepoxide, clonazepam, clorazepate, diazepam, lorazepam, midazolam, oxazepam, temazepam, and zolpidem through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The caffeine component may reduce the sedative effects of these medications. Green tea increases the levels of dihydroergotamine and ergotamine by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised due to the caffeine content. Green tea, when combined with herbs such as American ginseng, Panax ginseng, dong quai, feverfew, garlic, ginger, ginkgo biloba, or willow bark, may increase the risk of bleeding due to their antiplatelet or anticoagulant activity. Caution is recommended. Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of green tea, potentially potentiating the clinical effects and duration of caffeine action. Caution is advised. Guarana, when taken with green tea, may produce excessive caffeine-like side effects such as nausea, irritability, or nervousness. Patients consuming large amounts of caffeine should exercise caution. Quinolones such as ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin increase the levels of green tea by decreasing its elimination. This is due to the inhibition of hepatic clearance of caffeine. Caution is advised. Green tea increases lithium levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Lithium levels may rise following abrupt caffeine withdrawal. Caution is recommended. Carbamazepine, phenobarbital, primidone, and St. John’s Wort decrease the levels or effects of green tea by increasing its metabolism. This may reduce the effects of caffeine. Caution is advised. Green tea increases the effects of acetaminophen (oral, IV, or rectal) through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction is theoretical and attributed to the caffeine content. The clinical significance is unknown. Green tea decreases the effects of adenosine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Green tea increases the effects of abciximab, alteplase, anagrelide, antithrombin alfa, and antithrombin III through pharmacodynamic synergy. The combination may increase the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Mestranol increases the levels of green tea by decreasing its elimination. This interaction is minor, and the clinical significance is unknown. Green tea increases the effects of amphetamine due to the caffeine content, which acts as a CNS stimulant. Additive effects may occur when coadministered with other CNS stimulants. Caffeine should be avoided or used cautiously.
